newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Guerrillas say have Tajik govt troops surrounded.
newsitem.headline: Guerrillas say have Tajik govt troops surrounded.

text.p: Islamist opposition guerrillas have surrounded a battalion of Tajik government troops at an airport outside the disputed town of Garm, a senior opposition official said on Tuesday.
"The battalion is surrounded by our fighters," Jaloleddin Makhmudov, the opposition's representative on a United Nations-sponsored ceasefire commission, told Reuters in the Tajik capital, Dushanbe.
He said the battalion, comprising an undisclosed number of Tajik Interior Ministry troops, was surrounded at Garm airport, around 200 km (130 miles) east of the capital.

Makhmudov said an offer made on Tuesday by the opposition to let the government troops go if they surrendered their weapons had been rejected by the Tajik government, although this could not be immediately confirmed by Dushanbe officials.

Tajik military sources quoted by Interfax news agency said there had been sporadic fighting overnight. But Makhmudov and United Nations sources said the town, taken by opposition fighters on Sunday, was now quiet.
Renewed fighting in the former Soviet republic came days before planned peace talks between Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri on December 9.

Tajik government troops and Islamist guerrillas have fought a bitter civil war for nearly five years, leaving tens of thousands dead and many more homeless among the remote, mountainous country's 5.7 million population.
